question.text: The Battles of Breitenfeld and Lutzen were victories for the Protestant States over the Catholics in this war, which was ended by the Peace of Westphalia. This war is named for its duration.
question.clue: This war's Bohemian phase ended at the Battle of White Mountain, which saw a victory for Count Tilly.

swap.text: Through family ties, this Holy Roman Emperor also ruled Spain, the Netherlands, and Austria. He presided over the Diet of Worms, which outlawed Luther and the Reformation that had started during this man's reign.
swap.answerHtml: Charles V (accept Karl V or Carlos V; prompt on just “Charles” or “Carlos”; accept Charles I of Spain or Carlos I of Spain but do not accept or prompt on “Charles I”)
swap.clue: His general Charles of Lannoy secured the Treaty of Madrid for this man by defeating Francis I at Pavia.

question.text: The Utraquists' insistence on serving both the bread and the wine during the Eucharist contributed to a series of conflicts named for this Bohemian religious leader, who was executed at the Council of Constance.
question.clue: Prokop the Great led forces that pioneered the use of war wagons among this man's Taborite followers in a 15th-century conflict.

swap.leadin: After this ruler won the 1159 Siege of Crema, he attempted to boss around the future pope Alexander III. Alexander's refusal led this man to support Victor IV in his bid to be pope.
swap.text: Name this Holy Roman Emperor that was excommunicated by Alexander III.
swap.clue: This ruler drowned in the Saleph River during an invasion he undertook with Philip II Augustus.

question.leadin: Answer these questions regarding the Holy Roman Empire.
question.text: The next man to receive the title of Holy Roman Emperor was this man who defeated the Magyars at the Battle of Lechfeld. His coronation marked the beginning of the First Reich.
question.clue: Much of his ruling strength came from his namesake system of installing his own bishops, and later in his rule, he deposed John XII in favor of Leo VIII for the papacy.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the "first" Holy Roman Emperors.
swap.text: This man was the first to be crowned holy roman emperor in 962. He founded his dynasty after defeating the Magyars [MU-jars] in the battle of Lechfeld [LEK-feld].
swap.clue: He subjugated Berengar of Ivrea to rescue the kidnapped Adelaide, whom he married, making him King of Lombardy.

question.leadin: Name these ruling families important in German history.
question.text: From 1138 to 1208, this dynasty ruled over Germany, producing three Holy Roman Emperors, including Kaiser Friedrich Rotbart, better known as Frederick Barbarossa.
question.clue: The decline of this dynasty was accompanied by the rise of the papacy-backed William of Holland, and saw the short rule of Conrad IV and the young Conradin.

swap.text: The first king of newly independent Greece was a Bavarian prince of this name. A Prussian politician with this first name kept power by making melodramatic offers to resign, which persuaded Wilhelm I to retain him.
swap.clue: The fourth and final one was the only Welf to become emperor, but was defeated at the Battle of Bouvines, after which Frederick II restored the Hohenstaufen Dynasty.

question.text: In its aftermath, Frederick fled to Breslau and attempted to negotiate with Ferdinand. For 15 points, Christian Anhalt was defeated by the Catholic League under Tilly in what battle that ended the Bohemian phase of the Thirty Years War?
question.clue: Descartes may have been present at this one-hour battle, as an observer in the army of the count of Bucquoy.

swap.text: Tilly's first defeat in the war was in this September 17, 1631 battle where Gustav Karlsson Horn executed one of the first troop shifts in modern warfare. Gustavus Adolphus's troops killed some 12,000 Imperial troops at this battle in Saxony.
swap.clue: Another cavalry charge by Furstenberg drove off John George I and his Saxon troops, exposing the eventual victor's left flank.

question.text: Most of the radium for Vienna's Radium Institute was sourced from Jachymov ("yah-HE-mov"), a mine in this region. This region shares its name with a kingdom founded by the Premyslid ("prem-EH-slid") dynasty.
question.answerHtml: Bohemia [or Čechy; or Böhmen; accept Kingdom of Bohemia; prompt on Czech Kingdom or Czechia]
question.clue: A university in this region's New Town was founded by Charles IV, who was crowned after his blind father John died at the Battle of Crecy.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about times when people were chucked out of windows in Prague.
swap.text: The First Defenestration of Prague in 1419, which killed seven Prague town council members, was carried out by members of this religious movement, who followed the teachings of a heretic burned at the Council of Constance.
swap.clue: These people, led by Jan Zelivsky, threw Catholic magistrates out of a window during the First Defenestration of Prague.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the politics of the Holy Roman Empire.
question.text: A 1356 proclamation known by this name explicitly named the seven positions whose titles conferred elector status. A 1222 edict with this name ceded a number of rights to the Hungarian nobility.
question.answerHtml: Golden Bull [or Golden Bull of 1356; or Golden Bull of 1222; or chrysobull; prompt on “bull”]
question.clue: Emperor Frederic II was identified as the source of the 1218 one of Berne, considered a forgery, but definitely did issue one dealing with the holdings of Teutonic knights in Prussia named for the town of Rimini.

swap.leadin: This Holy Roman emperor has become a very popular figure in Czech culture.
swap.text: Name this twenty seventh ruler of the Holy Roman Empire who ruled from 1355 to 1378 from his home in Prague.
swap.answerHtml: Charles IV [accept Charles of Luxembourg, Karl IV, Karel IV, Karol IV, or Carolus IV]
swap.clue: The last Wittelsbach elector of Brandenburg was deposed by this 14th-century Holy Roman Emperor. This son of John of Luxembourg used Paris as a model in building the New Town in his capital and power base of Prague.

question.text: This league defeated at the Battle of Muhlberg was a militarized version of the earlier League of Torgau and was composed of Lutheran German princes who opposed Charles V.
question.clue: Taking its name from a town in Thuringia, this group was first formed by Philip I of Hesse and John Frederick I of Saxony.

swap.leadin: He put an end to the Ducal Revolts with the defeat of his brother Henry of Bavaria.
swap.text: Name this ruler who defeated the Magyars at the Battle of Lechfeld and was crowned by Pope John XII.
swap.answer: Otto the Great or Otto I
swap.clue: He divested Liudolf and Conrad the Red of their titles at the Diet of Auerstadt.

question.text: This Holy Roman Emperor was the nominal leader of the allied army against Philip at Bouvines. He was also the only Holy Roman Emperor from the House of Welf and was succeeded upon losing at Bouvines by Frederick II.
question.clue: This Holy Roman Emperor who struggled for control over the Holy Roman Empire with Frederick II Hohenstaufen ("HO-en-shtow-fin"). He was deposed following his defeat at the Battle of Bouvines.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about some assorted medieval biographers, FTPE.
swap.text: Ripping off Suetonius' biography of Augustus, this advisor to Louis the Pious composed his Life of Charlemagne.
swap.clue: The preface to this notoriously short man's most famous work was written by Walafrid Strabo.

question.leadin: This man was made a saint and posthumously declared the king of the Czechs after his death.
question.text: Name this knize and saint who was supposedly murdered by his brother, Boleslav the Cruel, in 935 CE.
question.answerHtml: Wenceslas I [or Wenceslaus I; or Saint Wenceslas; or Good King Wenceslas; prompt on “Wenceslas”]
question.clue: This son of Dragomir, the prince and patron saint of Bohemia.

swap.text: The Hussites' primary military leaders were Prokop and this man, who led the Taborites and was victorious at engagements like Horice and Nebovidy, but he died of the plague before he could see his side to victory.
swap.clue: This one-eyed general revolutionized mobile warfare by mounting cannons on armored wagons and led the Taborites to a series of victories over the Bohemian Crusade. After his 1424 death, Taborite leadership passed to Procop the Great.
